title: Is your long run too long? (reports Jack Daniels long-run limit)
population: General runners; rule attributed to Daniels' Running Formula, as reported by Running Magazine (the article was read, the book was not)
findings: Daniels's rule, as reported by Running Magazine: runners with under 64 km per week should limit the long run to 30% of total weekly distance.
Daniels's rule, as reported by Running Magazine: over 64 km per week the long run should not exceed 25% of the week's distance or 150 minutes, whichever comes first.
The article states the rule only in terms of weekly mileage or time and gives no 5 km or 10 km figures; the only race it mentions is the marathon as a general example.
limitations: Secondary source (magazine article, 2023-06-28, byline Paul Baswick), not the book: the claim is Daniels's rule as reported by Running Magazine, and applying it to 5-10 km is the engine's inference.
implications: A 30% share cap applies at low and medium volume: a 3 h week caps the long run near 54 min and a 5 h week near 90 min (arithmetic on time as a proxy for distance).
The 150 min cap is far above any 5-10 km need; the engine's 60 min 5K cap is stricter than Daniels and could be raised for high volume.

r1.note: The rule is located only in this magazine's report (30% under 64 km; 25% or 150 minutes above; byline Paul Baswick, 2023-06-28; re-read 2026-10-31). The article names no book, edition or page, and the book was not read, so the rule is known by report.

r2.note: Byline Paul Baswick; no credential for him was confirmed in an independent record. The rule's author, Jack Daniels, is named but his work was not read, so his standing is not what the claim rests on.

r3.note: Article dated 2023-06-28 with no modification date; the edition of Daniels's work the rule comes from is unknown, so the latest edition cannot be compared.

r4.note: A magazine quoting a book is one source. Higdon's intermediate 5K plan puts its long run at 35 to 47% of the stated weekly miles (the record's arithmetic), above the reported 30%; the conservative reading is the lower share.

r5.note: Population is general runners and the rule is stated by weekly distance with no race distance; the record's limitations label the 5K and 10K use as the engine's inference.

r6.note: Evidence level D, at the practice cap.
